title: Introduce policy-aging-evaluator with KMS consent fallback and compact audit index
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a policy-aging evaluator to enforce temporal constraints, a KMS consent fallback path for missing tenant CMKs, and a compact audit indexer for efficient residency queries.
description: Motivation: several customer audits and internal reviews surfaced two gaps: (1) long-lived RBAC grants need a first-class temporal evaluator to support automated expiry/aging rules, and (2) when tenant CMKs are unavailable/rotated we require a consent-aware fallback that keeps requests safe and auditable. This PR implements a policy-aging evaluator, a KMS consent-fallback adapter, and a compact audit index for residency-related queries. Design summary: implement a policy age evaluator that evaluates time-bound constraints as part of RBACv2 decisions; introduce a KMS consent-fallback that attempts tenant CMK usage and falls back to a service-wrapped key only when explicit tenant consent metadata is present; add a compact audit indexer that keeps residency and key-decision pointers for fast lookups and post-hoc compliance queries. Rollout plan: feature gated via config.policy_aging.enabled=false by default; staged canary on dedicated clusters for 48h; mission-critical customers will have policy_aging opt-in during first rollout; audit index is backwards-compatible and populates a new compact shard. Checklist: - [x] Core evaluator implementation and unit tests; - [x] KMS adapter with telemetry and consent-check unit tests; - [x] Compact audit indexer with retention trimming; - [x] Integration tests simulating missing/rotated tenant CMK; - [x] Documentation and ops playbook; - [x] Canary rollout plan in deploy/notes. Commits summary: 3 commits: 1) core: add policy_aging evaluator and decision hooks; 2) kms: add consent_fallback adapter and audit tagging; 3) observability: compact_indexer and index maintenance job. Files touched (high level): services/policy-evaluator/src/policy_aging.go services/policy-evaluator/handlers.go pkg/kms/consent_fallback.go observability/audit/indexer/compact_indexer.go api/openapi.yaml tests/integration/policy_aging_test.go docs/security/policy-aging.md deploy/helm/policy-evaluator-values.yaml Security considerations: consent-fallback only activates when request metadata contains tenant_consent:true and a signed consent_token is present; fallback path signs audit entries with fallback_kms_id and an explicit reason code to avoid silent key substitution; audit indexer tags each decision with locator keys for later verification. Performance: policy age check is O(1) per decision (cached TTL-based), added an optional async index write to avoid decision latency regression; measured median p95 decision latency increase <3ms in benchmark canary. Testing: full unit coverage added for evaluator conditions, KMS fallbacks and negative cases; integration test covers tenant CMK missing, rotated, and consent absent. Observability/alarms: new metrics rbac.policy_age.eval_count, rbac.policy_age.eval_latency_ms, kms.fallback.invocations, audit.compact_index.write_errors; alerting recommended on kms.fallback.invocations spike and audit.compact_index.write_errors>5/min. Docs: docs/security/policy-aging.md describes policy schema examples, migration notes and operator rollback steps. Review notes and conversation: Marco Li: "Can we avoid a synchronous write to the compact index in the decision path? seen potential p99 spikes." Reply (author): "Index writes are async by default; decision path only enqueues. I added a buffered channel and a bounded worker pool; see compact_indexer.go and observability metrics to track queue depth." Anya Becker: "Need an explicit test for signed consent token expiry handling." Reply (author): "Added integration case to tests/integration/policy_aging_test.go that covers expired/signed/unsigned tokens and expected failure semantics." Diego Ruiz: "Please add a small migration script to backfill the compact index for recent 30d windows." Reply (author): "Included backfill tool under observability/audit/tools/backfill_compact_index.go and documented ops steps." CI and pipeline: initial run hit a flaky integration test (policy_aging_test.go::TestConsentExpiry) that failed once; test was hardened and re-run; final CI status passed all checks including unit, integration (x3), lint, and builder image scan. Merge rationale and method: approved by reviewers after requested changes; merged using squash merge to keep history compact. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: ops run scheduled backfill job in non-prod, canary rollout started in dedicated clusters, monitoring dashboards created under Console -> Observability -> RBAC Policy Aging. Impact: enables teams to write time-bound RBAC policies and reduces compliance overhead for CMK rotations while preserving auditability and operator control.
